headline: Indian Markets Mixed as Nifty Rises while Sensex Dips on IT
why: Rising US Treasury yields and Fed rate hike concerns weighing on global sentiment.
Crude oil price surges creating inflationary pressures and prolonged weekly losing streaks.
Weakness in IT sector and Tata group stocks dragging down benchmark indices.
Global investor sentiment plunging to a 16-month low according to recent surveys.
whatHappening: Indian shares post their longest weekly losing streak in six years due to macro headwinds.
FCNR(B) deposits expected to generate around ₹5 trillion notional profit for banks over 5 years.
EPFO wage ceiling revision discussed to adjust social security thresholds without hard ceilings.
Air India plans to consolidate its budget aviation unit into the main group to trim costs.

stocksInNews.sources: Paytm in focus during market opening ahead of trading session
SBI reports FCNR(B) profit potential of ₹5 trillion for banks over 5 years
Weakness in IT sector and Tata group stocks impacting Sensex performance
IT sector weakness weighs on benchmark index movement
Longest weekly losing streak influenced by global oil price worries
Notional profits from foreign currency deposits projected to boost large banks
FCNR(B) deposit gains expected to benefit major private sector lenders
Trading cautiously amid broader market volatility and global rate hike fears
Defensive plays see mixed action as broad market sentiment declines
Auto sector sentiment subdued following global supply chain and automation cost news

summary:
Indian stock markets remained mixed with Nifty recording modest gains while Sensex dipped due to Tata group and IT sector weakness.
Markets faced global headwinds, including rising US Treasury yields, persistent crude oil price pressures, and rate hike fears.
However, positive projections for banking sector FCNR(B) profits and corporate restructuring efforts provided selective support.
